title: What's the Deal With Poop?
summary: Josh and Chuck explore poop: what it is made of, the Bristol stool scale (types 1 to 7), what healthy and unhealthy stool look like by color, shape, floating, mucus and odor, how often people poop, causes and fixes for constipation (fiber, exercise, hydration, squatting, bidets), the role of fiber in the gut microbiome, lactose intolerance, a Danish 700-year-old latrine, and a story of an Inuit man who survived being left to starve in the Arctic. The episode closes with listener mail about the 'Chuck and Josh effect' and sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and poop warning
segments.summary: Hosts joke about the title 'stool' and warn listeners the episode is about poop. They introduce why paying attention to your poop matters, mention fecal vomiting from severe impaction, and note a Danish latrine from about 700 years ago.

segments.title: Poop composition and the Bristol stool scale
segments.summary: Discussion of the average lifetime poop output and what poop is made of (mostly water, plus fiber, fats, bacteria). The hosts then walk through the Bristol stool scale types one through seven, with types three to five as the healthy range.

segments.title: Fiber, lactose intolerance and loose stool causes
segments.summary: The hosts explain soluble and insoluble fiber and their effect on stool. They describe causes of loose stool including lactose intolerance, artificial sweeteners, and gluten or celiac disease, with a tangent on milk and skim milk additives.

segments.title: Healthy stool: color, shape, and floating
segments.summary: Healthy stool is medium to light brown, soft and smooth, and sinks with a gentle splash. Light brown color comes from bilirubin. Floating stool may indicate fat malabsorption.

segments.title: Unhealthy stool: black, red, white, yellow, and mucus
segments.summary: Black or tarry stool can come from red wine, black licorice, or internal bleeding; red may be from beets or bleeding. Pale or white stool can signal low bile or be from barium. Yellow stool can relate to Gilbert syndrome, giardia or gallbladder problems. Mucus is normal in small amounts but a large amount is concerning.

segments.title: Stool odor and changes in habits
segments.summary: Stool smells because bacteria produce gas when digesting food. Unusually foul odor could signal malabsorption conditions. The key is noticing big changes from your own normal. Normal frequency ranges widely, from three times a week to three times a day.

segments.title: Constipation, impaction and hemorrhoids
segments.summary: Causes of constipation include travel, diet changes, hormones, sleep, illness, and age over 65. Problems include straining, incomplete elimination, impaction, and hemorrhoids. Treatment for impaction can include mineral oil or manual breaking up of stool or surgery.

segments.title: Fixing constipation: fiber, exercise, water, toilet posture
segments.summary: Advice includes avoiding laxatives as a last resort, eating whole fruits and vegetables for fiber, limiting processed food and sugar, exercising to strengthen the core, staying hydrated, and avoiding opioid painkillers. The hosts discuss squatting versus sitting on a toilet and products like footstools and bidets.

segments.title: Gut microbiome, fiber and diet
segments.summary: A Stanford study with microbe-free mice showed that low-fiber diets reduced microbial diversity and that recovery was only partial. The hosts argue modern diets are low in fiber and high in processed white foods.

segments.title: Poop as a weapon and an Inuit survival story
segments.summary: The hosts mention historical use of feces as a weapon and Soviet poop artillery. They then recount Wade Davis's TED talk story of an Inuit man in the 1950s, left with two dogs in Arctic Bay, who froze his feces into a knife to kill a dog for food and reached Pond Inlet.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener notes that topics covered on the show often appear in other articles the next day, calling it the Chuck and Josh effect. The hosts joke about a band name and sign off with web and social links.
